newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-HOLYFIELD IS COUNTING ON GOD BEING A FIGHT FAN.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-HOLYFIELD IS COUNTING ON GOD BEING A FIGHT FAN.

text.p: The question on Thursday, as it has been most of the week, is whether God will be working both corners of the Mike Tyson-Evander Holyfield title fight on Saturday.
All the talk about God this week is reminiscent of a schoolyard with kids in short pants running up to taunt each other: "Na na na na na, my God is better than your God. My God can beat up your God."

Holyfield all but says his God, of the Christian persuasion, will protect him, as the oddsmakers think he needs protecting, from Tyson's awesome lefts and rights at the MGM Grand Arena in what Holyfield seems to think is a Holy War for Tyson's World Boxing Association title.

Holyfield, who in recent years seems incapable of uttering a sentence without a reference to his deity, says the long-awaited showdown between the two fighters will give him a chance to show the world the power of God.

People, Holyfield insists, will say: "'Hey, this man believes in God. Let's see what God can do for him.' I know this (fight) is going to put a lot of eyes on me, and people are going to watch TV and say, 'I want to see what God is going to do for him against Mike Tyson.'"

Holyfield, 34, said earlier this week that when the going gets tough in the fight, which many people don't think will come close to lasting the scheduled 12 rounds, he will be able to draw strength from his faith in God.

It is only a strong faith that will allow a person to receive this strength, Holyfield (32-3) says, implying that Tyson, who converted to Islam while in prison serving three years for rape, will not get help from God.
"What? God don't like me? God don't like you?" Tyson said when told of Holyfield's remarks.

Holyfield, who will receive $11 million for the opportunity to spread The Word, said at Thursday's news conference/sales pitch/revival meeting: "I thank God for allowing me to be a vessel. I thank God for allowing me to change the world with this fight."

Tyson's co-manager, Rory Holloway, jumped into the battle for God's attention and said: "Holyfield's parading around town talking up giving the appearance of a good champion, (saying) good man, bad man, good man, bad man, trying to get that perception.
"What makes him think that God is only shining on one side of the street?" Holloway asked, to the whoops and catcalls of Tyson's entourage.
"He's right," Holloway said, "the world is going to change on Saturday. I just hope he's around on Sunday to see it."
Tyson's other co-manager, John Horne, of course, had to chime in with his take on whether God will be ringside. Surprisingly, Horne seemed to be a vessel for moderation.

"There's no doubt in my mind that there isn't a person in this room that God doesn't love. Everybody here's blessed to just to be here. Everybody's got their own way that God shines on them," Horne said
"In that ring, you got Mike Tyson, Evander Holyfield and the referee," Horne said. "The only thing about God's love is this: After Evander gets knocked out, God's still gonna love him."

The 30-year-old Tyson, who will be paid $30 million for the crusade, was more animated than usual while sitting through the often tedious portions of King's sales pitch for the fight and the undercard, which includes Michael Moorer defending his International Boxing Federation's heavyweight title against South African Francois Botha.

"I bear witness that there is one God and I bear witness that the prophet Mohammad is the prophet of God," said Tyson (45-1). "I'm just happy to be here and I thank Allah for helping me to be strong, and I'm looking forward to this fight.
"I know everybody's excited and are saying things a little bit over extensive. I'm just here to do my job," Tyson said. "It'll be an interesting night. I know you won't forget it."
Later on, Tyson, in answering questions from the floor of the arena, said he does not have "any one feeling" about the fight. "My objective is to hurt my opponent with my punches."
Holyfield, asked for his strategy for the fight, said, "I will be led by the Spirit."
